skill.name: competitor-tracker
skill.description: Use when the user asks to "track competitor influencer marketing", "see who my rivals partner with", or "benchmark my influencer program"; produces a competitor partnership roster, campaign and content-strategy breakdown, performance estimates, and a gap/opportunity list. Not for finding your own new creators — use influencer-discovery.
skill.summary: Compare competitor creator partnerships, campaign patterns, estimated performance, and strategic opportunities.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, emoji, and fixed relative documentation links. Two instructions intentionally run bundled Python connectors, and one accesses a public YouTube feed; these are expected features but create limited command and network exposure.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs agents to execute Python connector scripts that are outside the reviewed file set.
remediation.suggestion: Package and audit the connector scripts with the skill, validate all placeholder arguments, and require confirmation before command execution.

remediation.issue: The YouTube monitoring workflow contacts an external API or public RSS endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the destination before access, request user consent, minimize transmitted identifiers, and preserve the documented rate limits.

content.value_statement: Competitor influencer activity is difficult to compare across creators, campaigns, and platforms. This skill organizes evidence, estimates performance, and ranks strategic gaps.
actual_capabilities: Defines the tracked brand, competitor set, platforms, date range, and research focus.
Builds competitor creator rosters with handles, audience size, partnership type, and duration.
Breaks down campaign timing, platform mix, content formats, calls to action, and estimated spend.
Compares brands by creator tier, platform, engagement, content style, and relationship model.
Estimates reach, engagement, earned media value, and spend while labeling figures as estimates.
Ranks creator, platform, niche, and content-format opportunities from observed competitor gaps.
limitations: Results depend on public information, user-provided evidence, and available connectors.
Reach, spend, earned media value, and performance figures are estimates unless verified data is supplied.
Connector commands require a compatible host, bundled scripts, and optional service credentials.
Partnership rosters can become outdated and require a defined monitoring cadence.

use_cases.title: Benchmark a Brand Program
use_cases.description: Compare your creator mix, platforms, campaign cadence, and estimated performance against selected competitors.

use_cases.title: Map Category Campaign Patterns
use_cases.description: Review competitor launches, seasonal timing, creative formats, messages, and calls to action across a defined period.

use_cases.title: Find Strategic Openings
use_cases.description: Identify underused creators, platforms, niches, and content formats before planning the next campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Track One Competitor
prompt_templates.prompt: Track [competitor] influencer activity on [platform] from [start date] to [end date]. List partners, campaigns, sources, and clearly labeled estimates.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Rival Programs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [your brand] with [competitor 1] and [competitor 2]. Evaluate creator tiers, platforms, campaign cadence, content formats, and estimated engagement.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Campaign Shift
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze how [competitor] changed its influencer strategy between [period 1] and [period 2]. Cite evidence and separate observations from estimates.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Opportunity Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [competitor list] in [category]. Rank creator, platform, niche, and format gaps by evidence strength, expected impact, and implementation difficulty.

output_examples.input: Compare two skincare competitors on Instagram during the last quarter.
output: Competitor A used more micro creators and repeated partnerships.
Competitor B concentrated activity around one launch and larger creators.
Opportunity: test recurring tutorial content with underused mid-tier creators.
All reach and spend figures are labeled as estimates.

output_examples.input: Show which creators a rival partnered with this year.
output_examples.output: A sourced roster lists creator handle, platform, audience size, partnership type, observed dates, and evidence status.

output_examples.input: Find gaps across three fitness brands.
output_examples.output: A ranked brief identifies underused creator niches, weak platform coverage, missing content formats, and the evidence supporting each opportunity.

best_practices: Define competitors, platforms, dates, and evidence standards before collecting data.
Cite public sources and label every inferred metric or relationship as an estimate.
Repeat the review on a consistent schedule to detect meaningful strategy changes.
anti_patterns: Do not present estimated spend, reach, or earned media value as verified facts.
Do not infer exclusivity or partnership status from a single ambiguous post.
Do not compare brands across different periods or platforms without explaining the mismatch.

faq.question: Does this skill access private competitor data?
faq.answer: No. It uses public information, user-provided evidence, and configured connectors.

faq.question: Are performance and spending figures exact?
faq.answer: No. They remain estimates unless the user provides verified first-party data.

faq.question: Can it compare several competitors?
faq.answer: Yes. It creates side-by-side comparisons for your brand and each selected competitor.

faq.question: Which platforms can it analyze?
faq.answer: It can organize evidence from any specified platform, subject to available public data and connectors.

faq.question: Does it discover creators for my own campaign?
faq.answer: It identifies gaps and candidate opportunities, but dedicated creator discovery requires a separate workflow.

faq.question: How often should I run the analysis?
faq.answer: Choose a consistent cadence that matches campaign activity, such as monthly or around major launches.
